text:
A: Alright, mate. Craig.
B: Alright. Callum.
A: Where are you, Callum?
B: Wolverhampton. You?
A: Leigh. Near Wigan, Greater Manchester.
B: That's the rugby place, innit? There's a scarf on your shelf.
A: Yeah, Leigh Leopards. Rugby league. Go to a few home games with my dad. You're Wolves, I'm guessing, from the wall.
B: Yeah. Through my dad as well. Watch them down the pub mostly, cba paying for a season ticket.
A: Sensible. So what do you do?
B: Student. Computer science, second year. You?
A: I'm an instrument tech at a water treatment works near Warrington. I look after sensors, flow meters, control panels, that sort of thing. When something alarms, I go and find out why. I'm on call this week actually, so if my phone goes I'm sorry in advance.
B: What, like three in the morning?
A: Could be. Pump station kicks off, the alarm comes through, you drive out, it's usually something daft like a float switch stuck. You just stay calm and work through it. That's the job really.
B: That's alright, that. I'd rather that than meetings. My group projects are all meetings and I just want to get the code running, do you know what I mean.
A: Yeah, the paperwork side does my head in too. Do you do any of the hardware stuff or just code?
B: I build PCs. Cheap ones, second-hand parts, for mates and that. My laptop fan sounds like a jet engine though, so I'm not a great advert.
A: Ha. I've got a Raspberry Pi doing a bit of home automation. Lights and that. Leanne says it's pointless but it's fun.
B: Nah, that's decent. What you running on it?
A: Home Assistant. Mostly turns the hall light on when I get in from a callout so I don't wake the little one.
B: That's actually useful. Give it me, I'd have it doing all sorts.
A: Go on then. You do placements on your course?
B: Supposed to. Haven't applied for any. Everyone's on at me about it. The engineer woman I spoke to before this was on at me about it as well.
A: Yeah, no, I'd listen to her. I did an apprenticeship, and the lads who had something lined up just had it easier. Doesn't have to be fancy. Anything with your name on it.
B: Yeah, I know. I'll get round to it.
A: You play any football?
B: Five-a-side, Thursdays. When enough of them turn up. Got cancelled last week cos three dropped out.
A: Same with us on Wednesdays. We were short again. Always the same ones who don't show.
B: And the ones that do show don't track back.
A: Ha. That's me, to be fair. I'm thirty-five, I'm not tracking back anywhere.
B: Fair enough, mate.
A: What do you do for food round there? We get a barm from the bakery Saturday.
B: A barm? You mean a bap.
A: I mean a barm.
B: Bacon bap from the café by campus most mornings. Best thing about uni, that.
A: That's about it really, isn't it.
